item.title: Two-month-old baby living with HIV and TB highlights impact of Fiji’s HIV crisis on children
item.description: The organisation says the baby is the youngest patient in Fiji currently living with both HIV and TB, and the case should be of serious concern to the nation. Save the Children Fiji says as of 31st August this year, Fiji had recorded 438 TB cases, with 182 of those patients also living with HIV.
item.content:encoded:
The organisation says the baby is the youngest patient in Fiji currently living with both HIV and TB, and the case should be of serious concern to the nation.

Save the Children Fiji says as of 31st August this year, Fiji had recorded 438 TB cases, with 182 of those patients also living with HIV.

They say the situation among young children is also concerning, with 70 percent of children under five diagnosed with TB last year also living with HIV.

The organisation says 59 babies acquired HIV through mother-to-child transmission in 2025, while 67 new HIV cases were recorded among children under the age of 15.

They say 17 children under the age of 15 also died from HIV-related causes.

Save the Children Fiji says behind every number is a child, a family and a life that deserves protection, and these figures should not become normal.

The organisation stresses that the situation is not about blaming or shaming people living with HIV, saying they deserve dignity, treatment, compassion and support.

They say urgent action is needed to ensure people have access to HIV prevention, testing and treatment before they become seriously ill.

Save the Children Fiji is also calling for timely access to HIV testing, treatment and antenatal care during pregnancy to help reduce the risk of mother-to-child transmission.

They say children and teenagers need stronger protection and age-appropriate education, while parents should be supported to have open conversations with their children.

The organisation says government, communities, churches, schools, traditional leaders and civil society must work together as Fiji responds to the national HIV crisis .

item.title: Constitution Review Commission Report to be tabled in a special Parliament sitting next Tuesday
item.description: The Constitution Review Commission Report will be tabled in a special Parliament sitting next Tuesday. Minister for Information, Lynda Tabuya says the Speaker's Office has confirmed 22nd September at 11.30am for the special sitting.
item.content:encoded:
The Constitution Review Commission Report will be tabled in a special Parliament sitting next Tuesday.

Minister for Information, Lynda Tabuya says the Speaker's Office has confirmed 22nd September at 11.30am for the special sitting.

When we had asked Prime Minister, Sitiveni Rabuka after the presentation of the Constitution Review Commission Report to the President, he had said that "we are on a roll. We will have further deliberations before Parliament considers the Bill starting on 28th September."

fijivillage News has been informed that the first and second readings of the Constitution Amendment Bill will be done at the end of this month after the report is tabled next Tuesday.

The Bill will also confirm what the government has decided to amend in the 2013 Constitution after assessing the recommendations of the Constitution Review Commission.

The commission's report is yet to be made public.

As earlier reported by fijivillage News, the Constitution Review Commission has recommended a 41 seat House of Representatives or Parliament with 26 constituencies.

26 MPs are to be elected under the first past the post system and 15 through the proportional representation system.

The Commission confirmed that it has not recommended any reserved seats for women or ethnic groups.

The Review Commission is also recommending a 19 seat Senate.

The Commission is also recommending that the election of the country's President be done by a 6 member Presidential Appointment Committee.

The nominees for the President can be made by the Boselevu Vakaturaga, the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition, the Council of Churches and the inter-faith group.

Religious freedom is also guaranteed in the Draft Constitution.

The Commission has also recommended that FICAC should be an investigative body and the prosecution of the cases to be handled by the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

Some of the other recommendations arising from the 2013 Constitution review are the reinstatement of the Boselevu Vakaturaga; the reinstatement of the Public Service Commission to oversee the Public Service and personal matters of public servants; the continued use of “Fijian” as the national identity with a caveat that a consultative process is to be utilised so that people of Fiji can decide what their common or national identity should be, among other things.

The Supreme Court has already advised that the 2013 Fijian Constitution can be amended by the support of two thirds of Members of Parliament and a majority of those registered voters who vote for the change in a referendum after the parliamentary vote.

The National Referendum Bill is yet to be passed by Parliament.

Fiji has never had a referendum, and the Fijian Elections Office will need the Referendum Bill passed to move towards holding a referendum with the relevant questions to the voters if two thirds of MPs vote for the Constitution Amendment Bill.

item.title: Gau resident calls for road repairs as poor conditions disrupt weekly freight service
item.description: Akariva Vura, who is originally from Nacavanadi Village, says he operates a weekly freight service for villages and settlements around Gau. Vura says he transports hardware materials, groceries and personal belongings to the island every week, making reliable road access important for families and businesses that depend on the service.
item.content:encoded:
Akariva Vura, who is originally from Nacavanadi Village, says he operates a weekly freight service for villages and settlements around Gau.

Vura says he transports hardware materials, groceries and personal belongings to the island every week, making reliable road access important for families and businesses that depend on the service.

However, he says his truck has been unable to reach some areas in recent weeks because sections of the road have become difficult to use.

Vura says heavy trucks transporting harvested pine from Narocake towards Nawaikama have contributed to damage along parts of the road.

Insert: Vura on road conditions 15th Sep, 26

He says sections of the road have become slippery and developed a number of potholes, making it difficult for his truck to travel through some areas.

Vura says he raised the issue with the Fiji Roads Authority about three weeks ago and requested that the road be upgraded.

He says reliable roads are becoming increasingly important as development continues on Gau and more vehicles and trucks are being used on the island.

Vura is calling on the Fiji Roads Authority to carry out further repair and maintenance work so freight services and residents can reliably access communities around the island.

item.title: Rakiraki resident calls for 48-hour election campaign blackout period to remain
item.description: A Rakiraki resident is calling on the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Justice, Law and Human Rights to retain the 48-hour election campaign blackout period before polling day. Under the proposed Electoral (Amendment) Bill 2026, the current 48-hour period before polling day, during which campaigning restrictions apply, would be removed, with the restrictions instead applying on polling day.
item.content:encoded:
A Rakiraki resident is calling on the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Justice, Law and Human Rights to retain the 48-hour election campaign blackout period before polling day.

Under the proposed Electoral (Amendment) Bill 2026, the current 48-hour period before polling day, during which campaigning restrictions apply, would be removed, with the restrictions instead applying on polling day.

The resident, Tirise Nade, says people should be given enough time to think for themselves before deciding who to vote for.

Nade s ays the blackout gives voters an opportunity to reflect on their choices without being subjected to further campaigning or influence.

She says 48 hours is sufficient time for candidates and political parties to stop campaigning and allow voters to make their decisions freely.

Nade also raised concerns about any proposed increase in campaign-related spending, saying the financial burden should not fall on the public.

She says those seeking to be part of the system should be prepared to meet more of their own costs rather than relying on public funds.

Nade says the priority should be to support the public rather than place additional demands on them.

item.title: Batiki students forced to have half-day classes due to limited water
item.description: Batiki District Representative Tevita Tavodi says the school’s main water source has dried up, leaving it dependent on limited rainwater storage. He says boarding students from two villages returned to school yesterday after spending some time at home because of the water shortage.
item.content:encoded:
Batiki District Representative Tevita Tavodi says the school’s main water source has dried up, leaving it dependent on limited rainwater storage.

He says boarding students from two villages returned to school yesterday after spending some time at home because of the water shortage.

Tavodi says water use at the school is now being closely monitored as students continue with half-day classes.

Tavodi says the community believes the old dam has been there for more than 20 years and is relieved to have found water there.

However, he says the pipes connecting the dam to the school are old and will need to be replaced and repaired before the water source can be properly used.

Tavodi says the community has raised their water concerns during the Bose Ni Yasana for the past six years, but the issue remains unresolved.

Questions have been sent to the Ministry of National Disaster Management regarding possible assistance for Batiki. fijivillage News is awaiting a response.

When we approached Minister, Mosese Bulitavu today, he said he will respond later.
